panels.description: Total number of completed requests processed by vLLM since the last restart.
panels.title: Total Requests

panels.description: Total number of input prompt tokens processed by vLLM since the last restart.
panels.title: Total Prompt Tokens

panels.description: Total number of output tokens generated by vLLM since the last restart.
panels.title: Total Generated Tokens

panels.description: Current average output token generation speed in tokens per second. Higher is better.
panels.title: Avg Generation Throughput

panels.description: End-to-end request latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per model. Covers the full round trip from request received to last token sent.
panels.title: Response Latency (E2E)

panels.description: Time from request received to first token streamed back. This is the latency users perceive in Open WebUI before the response starts appearing. p50/p95/p99 per model.
panels.title: Time to First Token (TTFT)

panels.description: Time per output token after the first token has been sent. This is the streaming cadence users feel as the response types out. p50/p95/p99 per model.
panels.title: Inter-Token Latency (TPOT)

panels.description: Rate of tokens flowing through vLLM per second. 'prompt' is input tokens read; 'generated' is output tokens written.
panels.title: Token Throughput

panels.description: Rate of completed requests per second, broken down by model.
panels.title: Request Rate

panels.description: Requests currently being processed (running) vs. waiting for a free slot (waiting). Sustained queue depth indicates the model is saturated.
panels.title: Active & Queued Requests

panels.description: PagedAttention KV cache utilization as a percentage. Near-100% can cause preemptions — vLLM evicts KV pages and re-queues requests to free memory.
panels.title: KV Cache Usage

panels.description: Rate of requests preempted per second. A preemption means vLLM evicted a request's KV cache pages from VRAM due to memory pressure and re-queued it. Spikes here explain latency outliers and correlate with KV cache saturation.
panels.title: Request Preemptions

panels.description: Rate of completed requests broken down by how they ended. 'stop' is normal completion; 'length' means the response was cut off at max_model_len; 'abort' means the client disconnected mid-generation.
panels.title: Finished Reason

panels.description: Rolling average output token generation throughput in tokens per second. Reflects the current serving speed under live load.
panels.title: Generation Throughput

panels.description: Estimated cost for this traffic window if processed by OpenAI GPT-4o Mini ($0.15/1M input, $0.60/1M output). Prices as of early 2025 — verify current pricing at platform.openai.com.
panels.title: Est. Cost — GPT-4o Mini

panels.description: Estimated cost for this traffic window if processed by OpenAI GPT-4o ($2.50/1M input, $10.00/1M output). Prices as of early 2025 — verify current pricing at platform.openai.com.
panels.title: Est. Cost — GPT-4o

panels.description: Estimated cost for this traffic window if processed by Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet ($3.00/1M input, $15.00/1M output). Prices as of early 2025 — verify current pricing at anthropic.com.
panels.title: Est. Cost — Claude 3.5 Sonnet

panels.description: Estimated cost for this traffic window if processed by Google Gemini 1.5 Pro ($1.25/1M input, $5.00/1M output, ≤128K context). Prices as of early 2025 — verify current pricing at ai.google.dev.
panels.title: Est. Cost — Gemini 1.5 Pro

panels.description: Estimated cost rate in $/hr if this live token throughput were processed by each vendored model. Useful for projecting monthly spend. Prices as of early 2025 — update the query constants if pricing has changed.
panels.title: Estimated Vendor Cost Rate ($/hr)

panels.description: Distribution of prompt (input) token counts per request. This is the primary signal for how close requests are running to the model's context window (max_model_len). Watch p95/p99/max: sustained values near max_model_len mean clients are at risk of truncation or refusal. Compare against your model's configured context size.
panels.title: Prompt Tokens per Request (Context Window)

panels.description: Distribution of generated output token counts per request (p50/p95/p99/max). Combined with prompt tokens, this tells you total context consumed per request. A p99 at the client's max_tokens parameter suggests users are hitting their own output ceiling.
panels.title: Generation Tokens per Request

panels.description: Distribution of the 'max_tokens' parameter clients are passing in their requests. Shows what upper bound on generation users are asking for — useful to spot clients requesting huge ceilings even when not needed (which can affect scheduling and memory reservation).
panels.title: Client-Requested max_tokens

panels.description: Time requests spend waiting in the scheduling queue before inference begins (p50/p95/p99). Non-zero queue time means vLLM is saturated — correlate with Active & Queued Requests and KV Cache Usage. This is the latency component users can't see but feel as 'slowness'.
panels.title: Request Queue Time

panels.description: Time spent in the prefill phase — the initial forward pass that processes the full prompt before streaming begins (p50/p95/p99). Scales roughly with prompt length. This is the dominant component of Time-to-First-Token for long prompts. Correlate with Prompt Tokens per Request.
panels.title: Prefill Time

panels.description: Time spent in the decode phase — generating tokens one-by-one after prefill (p50/p95/p99). Scales with generation length. This is the dominant component of total latency for long outputs and is what inter-token latency aggregates.
panels.title: Decode Time

panels.description: Total time a request spends inside the engine (prefill + decode, excluding queue wait). Subtract E2E latency from this to estimate queue/network overhead; subtract queue time from E2E to cross-check.
panels.title: Total Inference Time (in-engine)

panels.description: Fraction of prompt token KV-cache lookups that hit vLLM's automatic prefix cache. High hit rates mean repeated system prompts, chat histories, or shared prefixes are being reused — drops TTFT and saves compute. Low or dropping rates can explain sudden TTFT regressions (e.g., after a prompt template change).

targets.expr: sum by (model_name) (rate(vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total{job="airunner-vllm-exporter", model_name=~"$model"}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (model_name) (rate(vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total{job="airunner-vllm-exporter", model_name=~"$model"}[5m])), 1)

panels.title: Prefix Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Distribution of tokens processed per engine iteration (p50/p95/p99/max). This reflects batching efficiency — higher values mean vLLM is fitting more work into each forward pass. Persistent low values under load may indicate small batches, memory pressure, or scheduling inefficiency.
panels.title: Iteration Batch Size (tokens/iter)
